key_insight: By expressing tetrahedral FE stiffness entries through edge lengths and dihedral cotangents, the paper extends Strang-Fix-style reasoning to prove discrete maximum principles for many meshes even when some dihedral angles are obtuse.
engineering_relevance: This relaxes strict mesh-acuteness requirements for Poisson simulations, making DMP-preserving finite element meshes easier to use in practical 3D engineering workflows.
method: Recast stiffness-matrix entries using edge lengths and cotangents of tetrahedral dihedral angles.
Apply structural mesh relations and simple trigonometric identities in the Strang-Fix spirit.
Show that the resulting stiffness matrices remain M-matrices for a broad class of tetrahedral configurations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports representative examples demonstrating that the relaxed geometric conditions still preserve discrete maximum principles.
watch_item: The result is still mesh-geometry dependent, so identifying or generating admissible tetrahedral meshes in complex 3D domains may remain challenging.
paper_title: Generalization of Strang-Fix remark for discrete maximum principles on tetrahedral meshes
